origins.section: Same-Typed Constructor Arguments Swap Without an Error; a Builder Names Each One
A Builder Checks the Whole Object in build(), Where Every Part Is Set
A Builder Used Again After build() Changes What It Built, Unless the Product Copies
HttpRequest.Builder Copies on build(), but a Reused Builder Keeps Adding Headers

recorded.prompt:q-postcodes-swapped: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-postcodes-swapped: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-postcodes-swapped: Page L69-71: "`customer` and `shop` are both `String`, so the swapped call matches the constructor exactly. The compiler checks types. A test that builds a transfer from its own literals and reads them back passes in either order." Applied to Shipment's two String postcodes, the call compiles and the tests pass, which is option a.
recorded.prompt:q-delays-in-file-order: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-delays-in-file-order: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-delays-in-file-order: Page L186: "When `to()` runs first, `fromAccount` is still `null`, and the check compares against nothing. A setter sees one part." The page's parallel case at L176/L182: setting the parts in the other order let the bad object through ("to, then from: Transfer[from=ACC-1001, to=ACC-1001 ...]"). Applied here, maxDelay() runs before any initial delay is set, so the check passes. The stem says build() checks nothing, so the policy is created with initial > max, which is option a.
recorded.prompt:q-encore-tracks: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-encore-tracks: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-encore-tracks: Page L295-296: "`Collections.unmodifiableList` stops the product's readers from writing, but it is a view of the same list, so the builder's writes still show through." Output L282-285 (view): the first product shows E-18 after the builder is reused. So tonight's playlist shows the encores, which is option c.
recorded.prompt:q-batch-header: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-batch-header: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-batch-header: Page L343-345: "The first request still has one key after the second was built: `build()` copies the builder's state into an immutable request ... The second request has two, because `header()` adds a value". Output L338: "reused:  first [po-17], second [po-17, po-18]". Carried on to a third push, the third request has all three ids and the first has only its own, which is option a.

recorded.prompt:q-postcodes-swapped:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-postcodes-swapped:b: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-postcodes-swapped:b: Refuted by L70-71: "A test that builds a transfer from its own literals and reads them back passes in either order. Nothing fails until the money is in the wrong account." The first half (each postcode lands in the other's field) is true. Only the claim that the tests fail is wrong, and that is the part the option turns on.
recorded.prompt:q-postcodes-swapped:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-postcodes-swapped:c: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-postcodes-swapped:c: Refuted by L69-70: "the swapped call matches the constructor exactly. The compiler checks types." The page's own call `new Transfer(customer, shop, ...)` compiled even though its variable names disagree with the parameters `fromAccount, toAccount` (output L65). The page never says outright that names play no part, but its example shows it.
recorded.prompt:q-postcodes-swapped:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-postcodes-swapped:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-postcodes-swapped:d: Refuted by L69 ("matches the constructor exactly") and L80 ("a five-argument call with adjacent `String`s"). That call compiled and ran (output L65-66), so adjacent String parameters do not make a call ambiguous.
recorded.prompt:q-delays-in-file-order:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-delays-in-file-order:b: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-delays-in-file-order:b: Refuted mainly by the stem itself ("`initialDelay(...)` and `build()` check nothing"). The page backs this up at L186: "A setter sees one part". In the page's own case, the setter that ran second (`from()`) did no check and the bad transfer was built (L182).
recorded.prompt:q-delays-in-file-order:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-delays-in-file-order:c: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-delays-in-file-order:c: Refuted by L186: "When `to()` runs first, `fromAccount` is still `null`, and the check compares against nothing." Output L182 shows no exception when the checking setter runs first.
recorded.prompt:q-delays-in-file-order:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-delays-in-file-order:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-delays-in-file-order:d: Refuted mainly by the stem ("`build()` check[s] nothing"). On the page, the original build() (L129-131) only calls `new Transfer(this)`, and the order-dependent version produced a transfer (L182). The idea that build() is where the whole object should be checked is the page's recommended fix (L186-187), not what this code does. That makes d an attractive distractor, but it is wrong for this scenario.

recorded.outcome:q-encore-tracks:a: Refuted by L295-296: "it is a view of the same list". Only `List.copyOf` "takes an unmodifiable copy" (L296-297). The reference table (L405) says builder writes show through for unmodifiableList: "yes".

recorded.prompt:q-encore-tracks:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-encore-tracks:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-encore-tracks:d: Refuted by L295: it "stops the product's readers from writing", which covers only the product's readers. The view output (L283-285) shows the builder adding E-18 after build() without an exception. The table (L405) says only the product's readers cannot write.

Its second half (the first request keeps only its own id) is true, so c is partly true.
